entities.summary:
The Battle of Friedland was a pivotal 1807 conflict in Eastern Europe that marked a turning point in the Napoleonic Wars.

The battle took place on June 14, 1807, near Pravdinsk, Prussia (now Cholmogory, Russia), pitting French forces under Napoleon Bonaparte against Russian troops led by General Mikhail Kutuzov.

The French emerged victorious, but at great cost in lives and resources, ultimately contributing to the Treaty of Tilsit, which solidified Napoleon's control over Europe.

The consequences of this battle would reverberate throughout the continent, shaping the fate of empires and nations for years to come.
